spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation of the Chapter of the Eighteen Thrones

---

** ¶1:** Eighteen governing principles exist for all who pr eside over the order of spiritual life , and they are established across eighteen distinct degrees of the mind . Nine of these operate in the outer states — the external and sensory regions of the human spirit where falsity has wr ought its corruption.

**¶2:** The first and supreme governing principle is Divine Love itself, which is the origin of all truth, the sovereign reality pres iding over every interior state of wisdom . It subs ists in its own essence alone, set apart from all derivative states, ne eding nothing outside itself. This is the first and highest principle , and it surpasses every other governing reality what soever.

**¶3 :** The second governing principle is the Divine Proceeding in its maternal function — Divine Truth as the matrix of life , from which every derived good and truth that has ever fl owed into the created mind takes its origin .

**¶4:** The third governing principle is established for the celest ial will in its original form — the first and in most human capacity for good, which hum il iated the entire primal enmity of evil that had established itself in the states of falsity and spiritual darkness.

**¶5:** The fourth governing principle belongs to the in most affection for wisdom — the love of interior light that is honored and cher ished among all elevated states of the spirit .

**¶6:** The fifth governing principle belongs to the great ordering power of Divine Providence, the supreme architect , who constructs an entirely new state of the mind — a new interior degree — as a dwelling for all goods and truths proce eding from the Divine, and simultaneously as a means of restraining evil and confining the advers ary and all its derivative powers within fixed limits .

**¶7:** The sixth governing principle belongs to the active Divine power that viv ifies and sust ains. It is this power that raised the celestial will out of its subm ersion in states of falsity, and that also ordered and constructed the external degrees of the mind — both for the purpose of purifying whatever wisdom had become entr apped in natural obsc urity, and for the purpose of binding the powers of the opposition so that they could do no further harm.

**¶8:** The seventh governing principle belongs to the medi ating function between interior and exterior states — the principle that governs the intermediate degree of the mind, and that directs all interior deliber ation and counsel.

**¶ 9:** The eighth governing principle belongs to Divine Truth in its redeeming and liberating function — the spiritual illumin ation that releases all interior affections from bondage and rest ores them to their proper order.

**¶10:** The ninth governing principle is that of the Divine Rational — the Divine Understanding itself — and all life that is purified from ent anglement with the natural and sensory mind returns at last to this principle and is received into it .

---

**¶13:** Three governing principles r eside within the doctrinal form that moves through states of conscious understanding — the vessel of clear spiritual light: one is the medi ating principle between interior and exterior, the second is the viv ifying spirit in its universal form , and the third is the active Divine power that orders and sust ains.

**¶14:** And again, three other governing principles reside within the doctr inal form that moves through obsc ure states — the vessel that belongs to the hidden will and to faith not yet made visible : the first is Divine Truth in its redeeming function, the second is the celest ial will in its original form, and the third is the recept ive innoc ence of interior perception . These six governing principles are established within the two containing forms — one carrying tru ths through the light of understanding, the other carrying goods through the obsc urity of the will.

** ¶15:** The seventh governing principle is established at the highest expanse of interior comprehension — the utter most firm ament of rational thought . The sovereign truth of celestial honor pres ides there .

**¶16:** The eighth governing principle is established in the lower rational mind — the atmosphere between interior spiritual states and the external natural life . The principle of Divine discernment presides there, which evalu ates every human state. Three paths are distinguished before it: one leading to spiritual death, which is the confirmation of evil; one leading to spiritual life, which is regener ation; and one leading to the min gling — the intermediate state in which good and evil remain com mingled and the outcome is not yet determined.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Eighteen [great thrones for all the fathers] exist and are appointed, which are established in eighteen places! While there are nine among them [appointed in] the outer aeons, they exist [i]n all the worlds of the damage.

The first throne is the throne of the Father, the God of [trut]h, the King of the aeons of greatness, the one who exists; who is established [by himself,] he alone, in his own essen[c]e, [dwelling] apart. This is the first throne [of all,] the one that surpasses all the thrones.
The second throne is that of the [gl]orious Mother of Life. She is the origin of all the emanations that have come to this world.
The third throne is constructed for the father, the First Man. He is the one who humiliated the entire first Enmity, which existed in the worlds of Darkness.
The fourth throne is that of the Beloved of the Lights, the great honoured Beloved of the aeons of greatness.

The fifth throne is that of the glorious Great Builder; the great architect who built the new aeon for a newness, for [a dwelling] for [the] fathers of light; also for a place of binding and a prison for the Enemy and his powers.

[The sixth thro]n[e] is that of the Living Spirit, the [glorious] mighty one, he who bore up the First Man out from the [land of Darkness]; who also set in order and constructed the world[s of the mixture,] both for a cleansing of the light, [and] for a binding [of the] powers of the Enmity.
The seventh th[rone is] that of the Third Ambassador, the king of the zone, also the master of all advices.
The eighth throne is that of Jesus the Splendour, who [is] the releaser and redeemer [of] all souls.
In contrast, these are the other nine thrones that are appointed in this world of the zone.
Three thrones in the ship of [the d]ay: one is that of the Ambassador, the second i[s that of] the Great Spirit, the third is that of the Living Spirit.

Once again, there are another three in the ship that [belongs to the night]: the first is the throne of Jesus the Splendour, [the second is that of] the First Man, the third is tha[t of the Virgin of] Light. These six thrones are established in the two ships.
Also, the seventh throne is established in the seventh firmament. The great King of Honour sits upon it.

The eighth throne is established in the atmosphere. The Judge of truth sits upon it, he who judges all mankind. Three paths shall be distinguished before him: one to death, one to life, on[e] to the mingling.
The ninth throne is the throne of the great M[ind, he to whom] … and all the [life] that will be purified from the world returns to him.
